attested.notes: Part D (Which?-style register) applied. The previous pass satisfied Parts A and C but described without judging, which is the Part D failure. Changes: the cost section now takes a view instead of listing charges. We checked the Fees Order on 8 August and state the consequence: a compulsory liquidation carries the 6,000 administration fee AND the 7,200 general fee, both payable, so 13,200 leaves the estate before a creditor sees anything, plus 15% of realisations, against 4,000 to 5,000 for a CVL. The arithmetic is named as not close. Hanging figures now carry consequences: the 800 preferential wage limit (the excess ranks unsecured and will not come back), the 15% realisations fee (the better the assets the more it bites), 2 to 15 years disqualification (published, searchable by your bank, and longer than most business plans). Strike-off gets the sceptical treatment a director actually needs: 13 pounds against 4,000 does not look like a decision, which is why it catches people out, and the 13 buys a filing not an outcome. Market scepticism sharpened on the debt-write-off cold callers: treat the language as marketing, they are selling a feeling rather than an outcome. Long paragraphs then split to the 150-250 target per Part B sequence, humanise first, split second. Opening materially unchanged since the recorded stranger read.
